script: Brag about how you'll just outbid me? Fine, I'll just outplay you.. I was at a charity auction for a very niche world this past weekend, and the vibe was all loud, brash, and oddly celebratory. Everyone was laughing, shouting bids, the whole place felt like a festival. There was a live auction and a silent one that wrapped up a few minutes later. Steve, the big name in this micro‑scene, was in the house. He'd been hitting every silent bid, bumping the price by a single dollar, like a ghost in the room. He'd moved from table to table, like a king with a thousand castles. I had my eye on a quirky home‑decor piece, something I'd bid on a handful of times. When I was about to raise my offer, a woman stood right in front of it, hands on the table, blocking me like a guard dog with a chew toy. Steve was right beside her, grinning. "Ah, you really want it, huh? Look, you see my name everywhere—just give up if you see Steve's name," I said, trying to keep it playful. Steve laughed, "Yeah, I've got three people watching the tables and bidding for me." I rolled my eyes. "Should I even bother to try bidding on it?" I asked, half joking, half annoyed. He shot back, condescending, "You can, but I'll just outbid you." I was like, "Okay, douche, I see you." I walked away, feeling the urge to prove him wrong. The live auction hit its final 60 seconds. Steve was nowhere near that item, so I sprinted over, heart pounding. A different woman—one of Steve's designated bidders—was already on the table. She shot up a bid, and I felt my pulse jump. "You're bidding for Steve, eh?" I asked. "Yeah…" she muttered, a touch embarrassed. "Got a top bid?" I probed. "No—he just told me to be sure to win it." She was like, "Okay, fine." Then it hit me—she was the bridge to Steve, the final hurdle. I kept my cool. When she finished writing the bid and dropped the paper, the auctioneer started counting down the last ten seconds. I grabbed that paper in one swift move, slapped the winning bid on the table with one second to spare. I threw my arms up like a champion, shouting, "WOOO HOOOOOO!" He may outbid me, but I outplayed him. I felt a pang for that woman, the one who didn't quite follow Steve's instructions. But, "Suck it, Steve, it's mine." This piece looks AWESOME in my house. …and I was still catching my breath, wondering if this was just the start of a bigger showdown.
